context.body: The ship is remembered not to retell Noah’s actions but to intensify praise of another person’s endurance.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: The writer compares a mother enduring her children’s torment to Noah’s ship bearing up in the world-filling flood.
observations.label: Noah’s ship becomes an image of endurance: action

observations.body: Flood, waves, storms, and preservation become poetic language for disciplined endurance.
observations.label: Noah’s ship becomes an image of endurance: response

payload.posture: Read 4 Maccabees 15:29–32 as ancestry and later memory evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The analogy selects the ship’s resistance to overwhelming waters without identifying the mother with Noah.
